speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you are presenting with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits or stool color regarding the abdominal pain? 

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, ESR, LDH, and CEA.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: WBC: Elevated, Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Platelets: Normal, ESR: Not in data, LDH: Elevated, CEA: Not in data

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that history; while tuberculosis is a possibility given your symptoms and smoking history, the specific location of your lymphadenopathy and the presence of abdominal pain require further differentiation. Given your earlier mention of a doctor suspecting TB, were you ever treated with anti-tubercular medications, and do you have any known exposure to someone with a confirmed case?

REQUEST TEST: Quantiferon_TST, HIV_Serology, and Abdominal_CT.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdomen_CT_with_contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Quantiferon_TST: Not in data, HIV_Serology: Not in data, Abdominal_CT: Dullness noted over the left lower quadrant; Splenomegaly detected; Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes observed on CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (likely Hodgkin Lymphoma given supraclavicular nodes, B-symptoms, splenomegaly, and mediastinal involvement).
